analysis.title: US Weekly Prospects (13 November 2026)
key_insights: October core CPI rose 0.30% m/m, the third consecutive upside surprise. The gains were broad-based, and the three-month pace of 3.7% annualized is the fastest since early 2025 or late 2024.

JPM estimates October core PCE at +0.29% m/m, which would put it at 3.2% y/y, equal to the May peak, and 3.5% annualized over three months. Unemployment is near recent lows, business survey price measures are near their peak, and PPI upstream pressure is elevated.
Market-implied Fed rate changes rose after the CPI and hawkish Fedspeak. The December meeting is priced at +27bp, up 8bp, and the June 2027 meeting at +81bp, up 39bp.

Governor Waller said a core CPI of 0.3% m/m or higher would justify considering a 50bp hike in December. Core printed 0.30% exactly. JPM still thinks a 25bp hike is more likely, but a 50bp move will at least be discussed.
Fed officials were mixed. Logan, Schmid and Goolsbee could be read as supporting hikes beyond December, Williams saw no signs of overheating, and Vice Chair Bowman was comparatively dovish.

The Fed made three changes to its 2027 calendar. The October 26-27 meeting becomes a Monetary Policy Strategy Meeting with no policy action, the December 7-8 meeting moves forward to November 16-17, and the calendar no longer tags which meetings include a Summary of Economic Projections. Whether the SEP is being eliminated is unclear, and JPM thinks dropping it would need wider FOMC approval.

JPM expects the December FOMC to hike, with the median voter anticipating multiple hikes next year. It sees a policy pivot away from the Fed's earlier stance of expecting disinflation without restraint.

Brent futures fell only $2 on the week to $96, against a recent peak of $118 before the midterms. JPM commodity strategists forecast an average of $71 in 1Q27, citing slowly rising oil inventories and Middle East exports recovering.

Core inflation drivers include supply chain strain, tech price pass-through into consumer electronics, accelerating supercore services, owner's equivalent rent and rising new market rents. The end of IEEPA tariffs and tariff refunds may be fading as a drag on goods prices.

The PPI core was a tenth below JPM's expectation, but the core intermediate materials PPI has accelerated in each of the last three reports and sometimes leads final demand goods by six to nine months.

Existing home sales fell 5.5% m/m in October to 3.75mn saar, the lowest since August 2010. The 30-year mortgage rate rose to 7.33% from 6.86%, and months' supply is the highest since late 2015. Median price growth slowed to 0.4% y/y.

Next week's US data are expected to stay soft on housing. JPM expects NAHB at 30, housing starts at 1.245mn with a rebound confined to multifamily, permits down to 1.385mn, and pending home sales down 3.0% to a new low.

JPM expects October retail sales flat (0.0%) against a consensus of 0.2%, ex autos +0.3%, and the control group +0.2%. That would be consistent with roughly no change in real consumer spending and supports a Q4 real spending forecast of 1.5% after strong middle quarters.
JPM's import price forecast of +1.1% m/m is at the top of the consensus range of 0.1% to 1.1%, against a 0.7% median. It would push the y/y rate to a cycle high of 9.1%.

JPM's global view rests on resilient tech and non-tech demand and sticky core inflation. It argues central banks and markets are near the end of a period of magical thinking in which solid growth was expected alongside falling inflation.

Global core inflation ex China and Türkiye re-accelerated to 3.4% annualized over the three months through October. JPM expects a broad round of DM central bank hikes next month, with a Fed divergence from other central banks possible next year as energy prices fall.

UK GDP grew 3% annualized last quarter and JPM raised its 4Q forecast by 0.5pt to 1.5%. It expects a February BoE hike with December now a close call. Euro area employment stalled in 3Q26 and growth is tracking above 1%.

The BoJ is expected to keep raising rates toward neutral at a quarterly pace through mid 2027. China's trade benefited from AI-related demand but domestic reflation is absent, and JPM's 5% annualized GDP forecast depends on fiscal easing.

In EM, JPM forecasts 25bp RBI hikes at each of the next three meetings to a 6.25% terminal rate with a risk of 50bp in December, and an out-of-consensus three hikes in Thailand next year starting in March. It expects unchanged rates in Czechia and Poland, modest easing in Hungary and 100bp cuts in Türkiye.

Romania 3Q26 GDP rose 2.1% q/q against JPM's 1% forecast, and JPM raised its 2026 GDP forecast to -0.2% from -0.5%. Headline CPI rose to 6.9% y/y and the end-2026 forecast went to 7.3%, with NBR cuts expected from May.

risk_factors: Further upside core inflation surprises, with upstream PPI and import price pressure not yet passed through to consumer prices.
Persistent energy price pass-through, given a Federal Reserve Board study showing higher DM inflation persistence and energy pass-through this decade.
Rising mortgage rates deepening the housing downturn.
A consumption downshift in 4Q as the tax stimulus fades and gasoline prices stay high.
Fed communication risk from the calendar changes and unclear future of the SEP.
China sequencing risk if fiscal easing does not arrive and bond-income taxation raises borrowing costs.
Central bank policy divergence and weaker EM currencies limiting the relief from lower oil.
vol_and_positioning: Market-implied Fed funds rate changes rose 8bp to +27bp for December and 39bp to +81bp for June 2027 over the week.
The October Michigan sentiment survey missed the later drawdown in equity prices, which JPM says could weigh on the November final reading.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict has kept business survey price measures rising and caused supply chain difficulties, and Middle East oil exports have recovered much of their earlier drop.
The end of IEEPA tariffs and tariff refunds may be fading as a drag on goods prices.
Political risks around upcoming elections and protests in Western Europe.
Romania's Niculescu government was approved, easing political tension, and budget negotiations depend on PNL support for PSD.
A possible Chinese tax on government-bond interest income could raise borrowing costs before domestic demand recovers.
Immigration enforcement is cited by builders as a hiring challenge, per the NAHB release.

tension_points.bull_case: The hawkish case is for a 50bp hike. Waller said a core CPI of 0.3% m/m or higher would warrant it, core printed 0.30%, and Logan, Schmid and Goolsbee could be read as supporting more hikes past December.
tension_points.bear_case: JPM's base case is a 25bp hike. Williams saw no signs of overheating, Bowman was comparatively dovish, and over six months inflation is within the range of the last couple of years.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Waller tied a 50bp hike to core CPI at 0.3% m/m or higher, and it printed 0.30% exactly, so JPM's 25bp base case is exposed to the December meeting discussion.

tension_points.bull_case: The firm run is hard to write off as a fluke. Survey price measures have risen since the Middle East conflict began, supply chain pressure is near its peak, and supercore has its highest three-month pace in two and a half years.
tension_points.bear_case: Runs of firm prints are not uncommon, over six months inflation is within recent ranges, shelter could cool again, and tech price pass-through could moderate.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued acceleration in the core intermediate materials PPI, which sometimes leads final demand goods by six to nine months, would favor the persistence view.
